name: Dennis Koshta
title: Dennis Koshta
description: Software engineer building AI systems, tools, games, and simulations. Projects, experiments, and writing by Dennis Koshta.
intro: I’m a software engineer at Bronco AI in San Francisco. I work on AI systems and tools, and make games, simulations, and websites on the side.
I’m interested in how AI can help us learn, discover, and build. This site is a collection of things I’ve been working on.

selected.description: Post-training experiments with OLMo-2 and Qwen2.5: supervised fine-tuning, preference optimization, and reinforcement learning on arithmetic tasks. Includes checkpoints, evaluation results, and a grader audit.

Five merged contributions to BusyCoq: twelve nonhalting proofs and one halting proof. I directed the AI-assisted proof-search work and submitted the contributions; Claude Code produced the formalizations.

Activation-steering experiments on Qwen3-32B. The completed screen found no change in stopping behavior across the tested interventions. The write-up covers the measurements, failed diagnostic, and limits of the result.
An adaptive learning platform with learning paths, practice, generated feedback, and checked answers. My work covers the learning flow, grading, content contracts, and progress tracking.
